etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French paver (“to pave, to cover”), from Vulgar Latin *pavāre (“to beat down, to smash”), from Latin pavīre (“to beat, strike, ram, tread down”).

definitions.definition: (British) To cover something with paving slabs.
(Canada, US) To cover with stone, concrete, blacktop or other solid covering, especially to aid travel.

quote.citation: 1970, Joni Mitchell (lyrics and music), “Big Yellow Taxi”, in Ladies of the Canyon:
quote.text: They paved Paradise and put up a parking lot.

definitions.definition: (transitive, figurative) To pave the way for; to make easy and smooth.

quote.citation: 2011, Rice Baker-Yeboah, The Animal Pathways 1-2, page 110:
quote.text: After two weeks Miguel began to circulate freely about the city in his truck, albeit with the long, chrome-plated pistol cocked and ready on his lap. It wouldn't be for three more years that Gonzo would tell Miguel about the secret leverage that paved his path to freedom.
